case_title: Rameshwar and another v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Political or land rival / prior enmity: appellant No.1 had a rivalry with the deceased; no relationship stated for appellant No.2
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (convicted accused). FIR also registered under IPC ss.452, 147, 148, 302 r/w s.149 and MP Dakaiti Act ss.11, 13; Dakaiti Act charges failed
weapon: Farsa (axe); firearms (rifle and a .12 bore gun)
evidence_type: Eyewitness; medical (post-mortem); recovery (cartridges, plastic pieces, axe)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted both appellants under IPC s.302 r/w s.34; life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine each; Dakaiti Act charges failed; all other accused acquitted
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under s.302 r/w s.34 and life sentence affirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (appellant No.2 only); appeal of appellant No.1 dismissed as abated on his death
neutral_facts: On the day in question, the victim had finished a meal at home, and then stepped into the courtyard to drink water. One accused, who had a rivalry with the victim, came into the courtyard carrying an axe. Several other accused stood at the door of a neighbouring house; some were armed with rifles and one with a stick. The first accused urged the others to kill the victim and then struck the victim with the axe. The victim ran out of the courtyard, but four men at the neighbouring door caught hold of the victim. The victim's mother came to shield the victim and was injured near her ear when she tried to take the axe away. The accused armed with a rifle fired at the victim, and the shot hit the victim's back, causing the victim to fall. The first accused is said to have taken a gun from a third accused and also fired at the victim. When villagers arrived, all the accused fled the spot. The post-mortem found one circular gunshot wound of 1.5 cm on the back, in the middle of the spine, with a fractured spinal bone and five pellets recovered from the spinal cord; the doctor opined that this injury was sufficient to cause death. The investigating officer seized a .12 bore cartridge, an empty cartridge and two plastic pieces smelling of gunpowder under a seizure memo. Eyewitnesses, including the victim's wife, father and two neighbours, gave consistent accounts that the rifle-armed accused was present. The first accused was arrested and, on his statement, an axe was recovered. None of the witnesses could say which part of the victim's body was hit by the shot fired by the third accused.
physical_harm: Victim died of a gunshot wound to the back (1.5 cm circular hole, fractured spinal bone, five pellets in spinal cord); victim's mother injured near her ear
premeditation_planning: Not expressly found as premeditation; the court found a shared common intention acting in concert between the appellants
motive: alleged: prior rivalry between appellant No.1 and the deceased
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent eyewitness evidence of PWs 1, 2, 6 and 7 placing appellant No.2 at the scene armed with a rifle; post-mortem evidence of a single gunshot injury to the back; seizure of cartridges and gunpowder-smelling plastic pieces
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses PWs 1, 2, 6 and 7 found consistent on appellant No.2's presence; contradictions on who fired were held not to matter given s.34
post_offence_conduct: Fled from the spot when villagers came (prosecution narrative); appellant No.1 arrested on 23.04.1984
trial_duration: offence: 08.01.1984; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25.06.2008; Supreme Court: 16.08.2019
legal_representation: Appellants: Nagendra Rai, Sr. Adv., with Rajesh, Advs. State: Rahul Kaushik, Ms. Bhuvneshwari Pathak, Ms. Shilpi Satyapriya Satyam, Siddharth Chakravorty (for Mrs. Swarupama Chaturvedi), Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime Case No.08/84); appellant No.1 arrested and axe recovered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: both appellants convicted under s.302 r/w s.34, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal of appellant No.2 dismissed; appeal of appellant No.1 dismissed as abated on his death
prosecution_argument: Oral eyewitness evidence and other evidence support the conviction; the High Court rightly affirmed it; PW-1's FIR statement is corroborated by PWs 6 and 7
defence_argument: No prior concert or meeting of minds shown for s.34; eyewitness depositions (PWs 1, 2, 6, 7) are inconsistent and contradictory, so the conviction is unsustainable
legal_principle_applied: Section 34 IPC requires (i) common intention among several persons to commit a particular crime and (ii) that, in furtherance of it, the crime was actually committed by them; a participant armed and acting in concert can be convicted with aid of s.34 even if another fired the fatal shot
other_sentence_order: Appellant No.2 directed to surrender within six weeks to serve the remaining sentence, failing which he is to be taken into custody
